title: Harbor Point Foods - Insolvency Signals

Credit hold already in place; no new orders since April. Bankruptcy-signal flag set. Given exhausted internal treatment and insolvency indicators, the realistic paths are a discounted lump-sum settlement to recover partial cash, referral to a collections agency or legal, or a write-off, each requiring Finance Controller approval per policy.

title: Harbor Point Foods - Outreach and Promise History
text: 2026-05-12: Firm dunning notice sent. 2026-05-20: Promise to pay 76,900 made by the CFO, then broken. 2026-06-18: Second promise (a 40,000 partial) made and broken. 2026-06-25 onward: calls and emails unanswered (unresponsive). Internal dunning path is complete (reminder, firm notice, calls, two broken promises). Required wait period before agency referral has elapsed. Recommendation: attempt a controller-approved settlement at roughly 35-45 cents on the dollar; if declined or no response, refer to agency or recommend write-off with full documentation.

title: Dunning Treatment Sequence and Wait Periods
text: Standard treatment progresses in order: (1) courtesy reminder at 3-7 days past due, (2) firm dunning notice once the balance ages past the next bucket or reminders go unanswered, (3) collection call to secure a promise to pay or an installment plan, (4) agency or legal referral only after the internal path is exhausted. Required wait periods: at least 14 days between the firm notice and any agency referral, and at least two documented contact attempts at the call stage. Never skip directly to agency or legal. If a dispute is open, pause dunning on the disputed amount and continue collecting the undisputed remainder on original terms.

title: Approval Thresholds: Settlements, Write-offs, and Holds
text: Settlements and write-downs: any discounted payoff or balance reduction requires Finance Controller approval before it is offered to the customer; document the rationale, the recovery percentage, and the alternative considered. Write-offs: permitted only for confirmed-uncollectible balances, with Controller approval and full documentation, after internal treatment and (where applicable) agency referral are exhausted. Credit holds: a specialist may place a hold when exposure exceeds the approved limit or a third-party risk score crosses the high-risk threshold; notify the account owner the same day and record the trigger. For strategic or high-value accounts, loop in the account owner before a hold or agency referral to protect the relationship.

title: Compliant Collections Communication
text: All collections communication must stay professional and within applicable fair-debt and privacy rules. Do not threaten, harass, or contact the debtor outside permitted business windows, and never disclose the debt to third parties who are not party to the obligation. Record every contact attempt in the communication log with date, channel, and outcome. When a customer states they are represented by counsel or in formal insolvency, route to legal and cease direct collection outreach. Empathy and accuracy recover more cash than pressure: confirm the balance is valid and undisputed before escalating tone.

title: Aging Bucket Recovery Play
text: Trigger: a balance slips into an older aging bucket (31-60 or 61-90) after reminders go unanswered, typically on a repeat-late payer. Goal: recover the cash and reset the aging without breaking the relationship. Steps: 1) Review the aging history and prior outreach log. 2) Send a firm dunning notice stating the balance, due date, and next steps. 3) Place a collection call to find the blocker and seek a promise to pay. 4) If the customer cannot pay in full, propose a written installment plan. 5) Set a follow-up checkpoint and update the cash forecast. Success metric: balance cleared or a kept installment plan in place, and the account moved out of the 60+ bucket within 30 days.

title: Dispute and Short-Pay Clearance Play
text: Trigger: a short-pay or an opened dispute blocks payment of part of a balance. Goal: resolve the dispute quickly and collect the undisputed remainder on original terms. Steps: 1) Open a dispute case capturing the disputed amount and the stated reason. 2) Gather backup (PO, proof of delivery, contract pricing, prior credits). 3) Route to the owner who can approve a credit memo or correct the bill. 4) Confirm the undisputed remainder is paid on schedule. 5) Close the case and document the resolution and any credit issued. Success metric: dispute resolved within the cycle-time target (10 days) and the undisputed balance collected on time. Do not dun or escalate the disputed amount while the case is open.

title: Pre-Write-off Recovery Play
text: Trigger: a severely aged balance (90+ days) shows insolvency signals or has exhausted internal treatment through broken promises and unanswered outreach. Goal: recover the maximum collectible cash and govern the write-off decision. Steps: 1) Confirm insolvency or that internal treatment is exhausted and required wait periods have elapsed. 2) Attempt a discounted lump-sum settlement (with Controller approval) to recover partial cash. 3) If declined or unresponsive, refer to a collections agency or legal per policy. 4) If confirmed uncollectible, recommend write-off with Controller approval and full documentation. Success metric: partial cash recovered via settlement, or a clean, fully documented write-off that removes a dead balance from active collection.
